results.rationale: ORM @Id on SqlBaseObject.id (inherited by all four entities). Exercised through canary_config and canary_archive: duplicate-id creates were rejected by application existence checks with HTTP 400 (no INSERT issued); PUT with an existing id caused Hibernate merge -> 'update ... where id=?' and read-back shows exactly one row, i.e. id identifies the persistent row.
limitations: metric_sets/metric_set_pairs ids are always server-generated UUIDs and could not be duplicated via the API.
Id is application-assigned (no generator); JPA save() merges on an existing id, so identity is enforced by the controllers' pre-checks rather than the ORM for create paths.

limitations: Behaviour depends on MySQL STRICT_TRANS_TABLES (enabled, default); non-strict MySQL would silently truncate.

limitations: Behaviour depends on MySQL STRICT_TRANS_TABLES (enabled, default); non-strict MySQL would silently truncate.
